# t18.2 — Design decisions and deviations

## The single root cause

`ApplicationPortFactory` used to build one `List<Path>` from two sources of very different
trustworthiness: directories the operator named on the command line, and directories discovered
inside the repository under review. After that concatenation the two were indistinguishable.

Every downstream consequence follows from that one line:

- **SEC-H2** — validators received "a path", so they could only apply one limit. Content authored
  by whoever opened the pull request was checked at the leniency intended for the operator.
- **SEC-H1** — the strict constants had no condition to hang off. They were written, then never
  wired, and stayed dead for long enough that they read as intentional dead code.

Both symptoms are unfixable while provenance is absent, which is why D1 had to land first. The
coordinator's ordering constraint (D1 → D2 → D3) is not stylistic: implementing D2 without D1
can only produce a single uniform limit, which is SEC-H2 with new constants.

## D1 — provenance is a type, not a convention

`AgentSource` is an enum, not a boolean, because the two values need names that survive being
read at a call site three layers away. `AgentSourceDirectory` pairs it with the path so the two
cannot drift apart in a collection.

Three choices worth recording:

**No defaulting overload.** `LoadAgentPort.loadAll(List<AgentSourceDirectory>)` has no
`List<Path>` sibling. Adding one would have saved editing ~10 test files, and would have
reinstated exactly the silent assumption the ADR exists to delete: the compiler would stop asking
"whose content is this?". Ten mechanical edits is the price of the guarantee; every call site now
answers the question explicitly.

**Fail closed.** `AgentSource.defaultWhenUnknown()` and `AgentTrustProfile.forSource(null)` both
resolve to `REPOSITORY_SUPPLIED` — the stricter side. A future caller that forgets to set
provenance gets tighter limits and a possible false rejection, never a silent widening.

**Trust is assigned in exactly one place.** `ApplicationPortFactory.loadAgentPort` is the only
site that decides `REPOSITORY_SUPPLIED`. Presentation tags its own paths `USER_SUPPLIED`, which is
sound because those paths only ever come from argv; the security-critical direction stays at the
composition root where the two sources are visible side by side.

## D2 — the constants were activated, not deleted

The five SEC-H1 symbols were unreferenced. The tempting move — delete them and report a cleanup —
would have removed the strictest bounds in the codebase and closed the finding by erasing the
evidence. They were moved into `AgentDefinitionPolicy` and given a caller instead.

`AgentTrustProfile` **references** them (`AgentDefinitionPolicy.MAX_UNTRUSTED_INSTRUCTION_SIZE`),
never restates the numbers. This matters more than it looks: see the findings document, where
restating them silently recreated SEC-H1 inside the very task that was fixing it.

`CustomInstructionSafetyValidator` kept `ALLOWED_CHAR_RANGE` and gained
`containsOnlyAllowedCharacters(String)`. Only the *decisions* moved to the policy owner; the
pattern knowledge stayed where it lives. `ValidationResult` was deleted — it is a result type
rather than a limit, had no callers, and `PolicyResult` supersedes it while additionally carrying
a rule ID, which D4's reporting requires.

## D3 — the contract as implemented

| element | USER_SUPPLIED | REPOSITORY_SUPPLIED | coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` | same | POLICY_RULE |
| `displayName` | ≤ 200 chars | ≤ 200 + charset | POLICY_RULE |
| `model` | prefix allowlist | same | POLICY_RULE |
| `peerModel` | prefix allowlist | same | POLICY_RULE |
| `systemPrompt` | ≤ 32 KiB, ≤ 300 lines | ≤ 8 KiB, ≤ 300 lines + charset | POLICY_RULE |
| `instruction` | ≤ 32 KiB, ≤ 300 lines | ≤ 8 KiB, ≤ 300 lines + charset | POLICY_RULE |
| `outputFormat` | ≤ 32 KiB, ≤ 300 lines | ≤ 8 KiB, ≤ 300 lines + charset | POLICY_RULE |
| `focusAreas` | ≤ 50 × ≤ 200 chars | same + per-element charset | POLICY_RULE |
| `dialogueRounds` | 0–10 | same | POLICY_RULE |
| `language` | allowlist `{ja, en}` | same | POLICY_RULE |
| `skills` | — | — | TYPE_SATISFIED |
| `rubberDuckEnabled` | — | — | TYPE_SATISFIED |
| `source` | — | — | TYPE_SATISFIED |
| `skillBudget` | — | — | INFRASTRUCTURE_INJECTED |
| *file size* | 64 KiB | **16 KiB** | file-level |
| *unknown frontmatter keys* | warn | **reject (closed schema)** | file-level |

Three points on this table:

**`language` is allowlisted at both trust levels.** It is not a trust question. The value is
concatenated into a template key (`"rubber-duck-initial-" + language`) and handed to
`loadTemplate.loadRaw`. Only `{ja, en}` templates exist on disk, so any other value is a lookup
failure at best. Restricting it closes SEC-L2 for operators too, because an operator typo should
also be a clear rejection rather than a confusing runtime miss.

**Limits count UTF-16 characters, not bytes.** t18.1 left this to the implementer. The existing
code measured characters; switching to bytes would silently tighten the effective limit roughly
threefold on this repository's Japanese-heavy definitions, converting a security change into an
unannounced functional regression. `AgentTrustProfileTest.limitsCountCharactersNotBytes` pins it
with an all-3-byte fixture, and mutation A confirms the test fails if the unit changes.

**`outputFormat` is validated after normalization.** `AgentConfig` prepends
`"## Output Format\n\n"` when the value lacks a heading, so the bound applies to the stored value,
not the file text. This is deliberate — the bound exists to cap what reaches the model, and the
model sees the normalized text — and is now pinned by two tests so it cannot be "fixed" by
accident.

## D4 — rejection is survivable and unconditionally visible

One bad definition previously risked the whole load. Now `AgentConfigLoader` records an
`AgentRejection` (filename, provenance, rule ID, reason), continues with the remaining files, and
returns an `AgentLoadReport`.

The summary line is emitted **unconditionally** — INFO at zero rejections, WARN above zero. A
summary that only appears when something is wrong cannot be distinguished from a summary that
failed to run; emitting it always means its absence is itself a signal.
`AgentLoadRejectionReportingTest.summaryEmittedWithNoRejections` exists solely to hold that line,
and mutation D confirms it fails the moment the summary becomes conditional.

ADR-0007 requires the summary to survive `--quiet`. **No `quiet` flag exists anywhere in
`src/main/java`**, so the clause is vacuously satisfied today; the constraint is recorded here so
that whoever adds such a flag exempts this line.

## Deviations from ADR-0007

| ADR text | As implemented | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D3 lists 13 `AgentConfig` elements | 14 | Measured via `getRecordComponents()`. `AgentSchemaCoverageTest` derives the count reflectively and fails if any element lacks a verdict, so the table cannot drift again. Architect notified; the ADR is theirs to amend. |
| D2 implies the dead constants may be consolidated | Kept and activated | Deleting them removes the strictest bounds in the codebase. Per the coordinator, deletion is an explicit regression. |
| D4 "must not be suppressible by `--quiet`" | Vacuous | No such flag exists. Recorded rather than silently skipped. |
